topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(1), how long does a license granted by the board entitle the holder to act as a broker or salesperson?
choice_a: Until the applicable renewal date specified under s. 440.08(2)(a)
choice_b: For exactly two years from the date of issuance
choice_c: Until the licensee's continuing education certificate expires
choice_d: Indefinitely, unless the board affirmatively revokes it
explanation: Section 452.12(1) states that a license entitles the holder to act as a broker or salesperson 'until the applicable renewal date specified under s. 440.08 (2) (a).'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(2)(a), what condition must a business entity meet before a broker's license may be issued to it?
choice_a: It must submit financial statements audited by a licensed CPA
choice_b: It must have at least one business representative licensed as a broker
choice_c: It must be registered with the Board of Regents of the UW System
choice_d: It must employ at least three licensed salespersons
explanation: The text provides: 'A broker's license may be issued to a business entity if the business entity has at least one business representative licensed as a broker.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: According to Wis. Stat. 452.12(2)(a), what must a broker obtain before acting as a business representative for more than one business entity?
choice_a: Approval from the Board of Regents of the University of Wisconsin System
choice_b: A separate salesperson's license for each additional entity
choice_c: The express, written consent of each business entity for which the broker desires to act as a business representative
choice_d: A public hearing before the Real Estate Examining Board
explanation: The statute says a broker may act as a business representative for more than one business entity 'if the broker obtains the express, written consent of each business entity for which the broker desires to act as a business representative.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(2)(c), within how many days after the effective date of a change in a business entity's business representatives must the change be reported to the board?
explanation: The text states: 'If there is a change in any of the business representatives, the change shall be reported to the board, on the same form, within 30 days after the effective date of the change.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(3), when is a firm responsible for the brokerage services provided on its behalf by an associated licensee?
choice_a: Only to the extent the firm fails to comply with s. 452.132 and any rules promulgated under s. 452.07(1m) with respect to that licensee
choice_b: Whenever the licensee commits any error, regardless of the firm's own compliance
choice_c: Only if the firm has fewer than five associated licensees
choice_d: Never, because licensees are always solely responsible for their own conduct
explanation: The text limits firm responsibility: subject to s. 452.139(3), 'a firm is responsible for the brokerage services provided on behalf of the firm by a licensee associated with the firm only to the extent that the firm fails to comply with s. 452.132 and any rules promulgated under s. 452.07 (1m) with respect to that licensee.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(4), what must the board include in the register it maintains under s. 440.035(1m)(d)?
choice_a: A list of every currently active broker and salesperson in the state
choice_b: The names of all persons whose licenses issued under ch. 452 were revoked within the past 2 years
choice_c: The continuing education transcripts of all licensees
choice_d: The trade names registered by all licensed business entities
explanation: Section 452.12(4) requires the board to include in its register 'the names of all persons whose licenses issued under this chapter were revoked within the past 2 years,' and states the register is available for purchase at cost.

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(5)(a), what happens to $10 of each renewal fee received by the department?
choice_a: It is refunded to the licensee once renewal is confirmed
choice_b: It is placed in a disciplinary enforcement fund for the Real Estate Examining Board
choice_c: It is paid to the Board of Regents of the University of Wisconsin System for research and educational, public outreach, and grant activities
choice_d: It is credited toward the licensee's next renewal fee
explanation: The text states the department 'shall pay $10 of each renewal fee received under this paragraph to the Board of Regents of the University of Wisconsin System for research and educational, public outreach, and grant activities under s. 36.25 (34).'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: A salesperson does not file a renewal application by the renewal date, and the renewal is not granted. Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(5)(b), what is the consequence?
choice_a: The salesperson may continue working under a 90-day grace period
choice_b: The salesperson's license automatically converts to inactive status
choice_c: The salesperson must immediately retake the licensing examination
choice_d: The salesperson may not engage in any of the activities covered by the license until the license is renewed or a new license is issued
explanation: Section 452.12(5)(b) provides that if a renewal application for an individual license is not filed by the renewal date, or the renewal is not granted, 'the applicant may not engage in any of the activities covered by the license until the license is renewed or a new license is issued.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(5)(bm)3, after a firm's license renewal is not granted and the business representative notifies a licensee associated with the firm, what must the business representative do next?
choice_a: Within 10 days after notifying the licensee, file with the department a notice of termination for that licensee on a form prescribed by the department
choice_b: Immediately surrender the licensee's pocket card to the Board of Regents
choice_c: Wait 60 days before taking any further action regarding the licensee
choice_d: Report the matter directly to the Board of Regents of the University of Wisconsin System
explanation: The text requires that the business representative for the firm, 'within 10 days after notifying a licensee, file with the department a notice of termination for each such licensee on a form prescribed by the department.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(5)(c), what must each individual broker or salesperson submit at the time of renewal?
choice_a: A criminal background check completed within the prior six months
choice_b: Proof of attendance at and successful completion of continuing education programs or courses approved under s. 452.05(1)(g)
choice_c: A signed non-compete agreement with their firm
choice_d: Evidence of professional liability insurance coverage
explanation: Section 452.12(5)(c) states that at renewal, each individual broker or salesperson 'shall submit proof of attendance at and successful completion of continuing education programs or courses approved under s. 452.05 (1) (g).'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 23.02, within how many days of changing their name or moving from their last address on file must a licensee notify the department in writing?
explanation: REEB 23.02 requires a licensee who changes the name on a current license or moves from the last address provided to the department to 'notify the department in writing of the new name or address within 30 days of the change.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 23.04, when may a licensed broker business entity begin conducting business under a different business type?
choice_a: Immediately upon submitting the application, before the fee is paid
choice_b: After giving the department 30 days' written notice
choice_c: As soon as the board verbally approves the change
choice_d: Only after a new license under the new business type has been issued
explanation: REEB 23.04(2) states that 'a broker business entity shall not engage in real estate activities under a different business type until a new license is issued,' and REEB 23.04(1) requires the entity to apply for and be issued that new license upon payment of the fee.
